files.lesson.md: --- order: 39 unit: trig10 node: AC9M10M03 n3 uses: [AC9M10M03 n1, AC9M8M06 n1] assumes: [AC9M8M06 n1, AC9M8M06 n2, AC9M9M03 n2] connection: box-diagonal title: The triangle inside summary: "To find a length inside a box, find a right-angled triangle in it: the floor first, then the one standing up on the floor diagonal. Pythagoras twice, or trigonometry for an angle." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "The umbrella is longer than any side of the suitcase. Will it go in?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8396 url: http://127.0.0.1:8396/index.html readySelector: "#board" layout: full --- A suitcase is 80 cm long, 50 cm wide and 30 cm deep inside (made up for the task). You have a 120 cm umbrella. Will it fit in the suitcase? Have a guess before you read on, and we'll come back to it at the end. ## Predict: will it fit ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to yes or no shows who thinks the longest line in a box is its longest side, and who knows a corner-to-corner line can be longer." check: type: predict q: "The umbrella is 120 cm long. The suitcase is 80 cm long, 50 cm wide and 30 cm deep inside. Will the umbrella fit?" options: - "No: even corner to corner it's too short" - "Yes: it fits corner to corner" - "No: it's longer than every side, so it can't" - "Yes: 80 + 50 + 30 is more than 120" actual: "No. The longest line inside a box runs from one bottom corner to the opposite top corner. That's longer than any side, but here it's still shorter than 120 cm. We'll find out how much." ``` ## Run: the line corner to corner ```step stage: run insight: "The board draws two right-angled triangles in the box: one flat on the floor, and one standing up on the floor diagonal. The long line is the longest side of the second." try: { playground: board, starter: "box.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Make the box $2$ by $3$ by $6$. Read the floor diagonal and the space diagonal.", when: "x = 2 and y = 3 and z = 6" } ``` Slide the sides. The grey triangle lies on the floor. The red triangle stands up on the floor diagonal. Which sides of each are known? ## Investigate: two triangles ```step stage: investigate insight: "The space diagonal is the longest side of a triangle whose shorter sides are the floor diagonal and the height. Sam adds those two sides instead of using Pythagoras again, and reaches the wrong decision." tasks: - check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A fish tank is 90 cm long, 40 cm wide and 50 cm high (made up for the task). What is the longest straight rod that fits inside? (1 decimal place)" steps: - ["Floor first: $\\sqrt{90^2 + 40^2} = \\sqrt{9700}$", "draw the triangle on the floor and find its hypotenuse"] - ["Then up: $\\sqrt{9700 + 50^2} = \\sqrt{12\\,200}$", "the floor diagonal and the height are the shorter sides of the second triangle"] - ["$\\sqrt{12\\,200} = 110.5$ cm", "work it out"] answer: "110.5" answerLabel: "Longest rod (cm)" tolerance: 0.2 feedback: - ["180", "That adds the three sides. The rod takes a shortcut across the tank."] - ["103", "That leaves out the 40 cm width. The floor diagonal uses the length and the width, then the height goes in the second triangle."] criteria: - "I found the floor diagonal first." - "I used the floor diagonal and the height as the two shorter sides of the second triangle." - "My answer is longer than every side of the tank." explain: "Floor diagonal √(90² + 40²) = √9700. Then √(9700 + 50²) = √12 200 = 110.5 cm." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#sam" text: "Sam checks whether the umbrella fits. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: diagonal-legs-added explain: "Line 3: the floor diagonal and the height are the two shorter sides of a right-angled triangle, so Pythagoras again: √(94.3² + 30²) = 99.0 cm. Adding gives 124.3 cm, which is longer than the real diagonal, and makes the umbrella look as if it fits." - check: type: question q: "In the second triangle, the one standing up in the box, which two sides are the shorter sides?" options: - "The floor diagonal and the height" - "The length and the width" - "The length and the height" - "The floor diagonal and the width" answer: 0 feedback: - null - "The length and the width are the shorter sides of the first triangle, the one on the floor." - "The length and the height don't meet at a right angle with the diagonal as the hypotenuse." - "The width is on the floor, so it isn't part of the standing triangle." explain: "The standing triangle has the floor diagonal along the bottom and the height up the side. The space diagonal is its hypotenuse." ``` ### Two steps Here is one with a room. ```worked \text{floor} = \sqrt{6^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{52} :: The first triangle lies flat on the floor. Its shorter sides are the length and the width. \text{pole} = \sqrt{52 + 3^2} = \sqrt{61} :: The second triangle stands up. Its shorter sides are the floor diagonal and the height. \sqrt{61} = 7.8 :: The longest pole that fits is about 7.8 m. ``` A storeroom is 6 m long, 4 m wide and 3 m high. The longest straight pole that fits from a floor corner to the opposite ceiling corner is about 7.8 m. Now try one on paper: a fish tank, 90 cm by 40 cm by 50 cm. Draw the floor triangle first. ### Find the mistake Read Sam's working. What kind of triangle is the second one? ### The standing triangle ## Modify: change the box ```step stage: modify insight: "Changing the box: a different suitcase, the angle the line makes with the floor (trigonometry in the second triangle), and a cube." try: { playground: board, starter: "box.yml#vary", height: 600 } tasks: - hint: ["Floor diagonal first.", "70² + 50² + 40² = 9000."] check: { type: number, q: "A box is $70$ cm by $50$ cm by $40$ cm. How long is the longest straight line inside it? (1 decimal place)", answer: 94.9, tolerance: 0.15, explain: "70² + 50² = 7400, plus 40² = 9000, and √9000 = 94.9 cm." } - hint: ["Draw the standing triangle.", "The height, 30 cm, is opposite the angle at the floor."] check: { type: number, q: "In the 80 by 50 by 30 suitcase, the floor diagonal is $94.3$ cm. At what angle to the floor does the longest line slope? (1 decimal place)", answer: 17.6, tolerance: 0.15, feedback: [["72.4", "That's the angle at the top. The angle to the floor has the 30 cm height opposite it."]], explain: "In the standing triangle the height 30 is opposite the angle at the floor and the floor diagonal 94.3 is adjacent: tan t = 30 ÷ 94.3, so t = 17.6°." } smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "In the standing triangle, what is opposite ÷ adjacent for the angle at the floor? (3 decimal places)", answer: 0.318, tolerance: 0.002, explain: "The height 30 is opposite and the floor diagonal 94.3 is adjacent: 30 ÷ 94.3 = 0.318." } - hint: ["A cube has all three sides equal.", "10² + 10² + 10² = 300."] check: { type: number, q: "Edge case: a cube has sides of $10$ cm. How long is its longest straight line? (1 decimal place)", answer: 17.3, tolerance: 0.1, explain: "10² + 10² + 10² = 300, and √300 = 17.3 cm: about 1.73 times a side." } ``` ### Another box ### The slope of the line ### A cube ## Practise: lines inside boxes ```step stage: practise insight: "Floor first, then up, for rooms and boxes, and a bearing review." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A room is $5$ m long, $4$ m wide and $3$ m high. How far is it from a floor corner to the opposite ceiling corner? (1 decimal place)" answer: 7.1 tolerance: 0.05 explain: "5² + 4² + 3² = 50, and √50 = 7.07, about 7.1 m." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "First, what is the floor diagonal squared? $5^2 + 4^2$", answer: 41, explain: "25 + 16 = 41." } - check: type: number q: "A box is $12$ cm by $9$ cm by $8$ cm. How long is its longest straight line, in cm?" answer: 17 explain: "12² + 9² = 225, so the floor diagonal is 15. Then 15² + 8² = 289, and √289 = 17 cm." - check: type: question q: "Review: which bearing is due south?" options: ["180°", "090°", "270°", "000°"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "090° is due east.", "270° is due west.", "000° is due north."] explain: "Bearings go clockwise from north: 090° east, 180° south, 270° west." ``` ### The room ### The box ### Review Bearings, from the last lesson. ## Make: the umbrella ```step stage: make insight: "Back to the suitcase: the longest line, then the decision, and what the number leaves out." tasks: - hint: ["Floor diagonal, then the standing triangle.", "80² + 50² + 30²."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "The suitcase is 80 cm by 50 cm by 30 cm inside. How long is the longest straight line inside it? (1 decimal place. The sizes are made up for the task.)" steps: - ["Floor first: $\\sqrt{80^2 + 50^2} = \\sqrt{8900}$", "draw the triangle on the floor"] - ["Then up: $\\sqrt{8900 + 30^2} = \\sqrt{9800}$", "the floor diagonal and the height are the shorter sides of the standing triangle"] - ["$\\sqrt{9800} = 99.0$ cm", "work it out"] answer: "99.0" answerLabel: "Longest line (cm)" tolerance: 0.1 feedback: - ["160", "That adds the sides. The line takes a shortcut across the box."] - ["124.3", "That adds 94.3 and 30. The second triangle needs Pythagoras too."] criteria: - "I found the floor diagonal first." - "I used the floor diagonal and the height in the second triangle." - "My answer is longer than the longest side, 80, but not as long as 80 + 50 + 30." explain: "√(80² + 50²) = √8900, then √(8900 + 30²) = √9800 = 99.0 cm." - check: type: question q: "The longest line inside the suitcase is 99 cm. What can you say about the 120 cm umbrella?" options: - "It doesn't fit, and it wouldn't even if the suitcase were completely empty" - "It fits, because 99 cm is nearly 120 cm" - "It fits if you bend it" - "It doesn't fit, but only because of the clothes" answer: 0 feedback: - null - "99 cm is less than 120 cm. Nearly doesn't fit." - "A rigid umbrella can't be bent, and it needs to fit with its thickness as well." - "The empty suitcase has a 99 cm longest line. Clothes only make it worse." explain: "No straight line inside the suitcase is longer than 99 cm, so a rigid 120 cm umbrella can't fit. (A real umbrella also has some thickness, which only makes it harder.)" ``` ### The longest line Back to the suitcase. Work this out on paper first, then type your answer. ### The decision **Also used in** - **Packing and building.** The longest rod in a box, a cable across a room, a pole in a tent: each is a space diagonal. - **Looking up, looking down.** The slope of the line in the standing triangle is an angle of elevation, from the floor corner. ```teacher summary: Students find the right-angled triangle inside a box, floor first and then the one standing on the floor diagonal, and use Pythagoras twice, or trigonometry for the slope of the line (AC9M10M03, node 3). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can find the right-angled triangle on the floor of a box and the one standing up inside it. - I can find the longest line inside a box with Pythagoras twice. - I can find the angle that line makes with the floor. struggle: "Seeing the second triangle. Ask: what does the floor diagonal become in the standing triangle? Point to the floor diagonal and to the height." before: > Do the Run board yourself first (the space3d board's diagonal view). Students need Looking up, looking down and Pythagoras from Year 8. The one idea: a 3D problem is two 2D problems, with the answer to the first inside the second. This relies on drawing the triangle clearly, as in Looking up, looking down; students who struggle there will struggle here. The common mistake is Sam's: adding the floor diagonal and the height instead of using Pythagoras again. It makes the umbrella look as if it fits. The sizes (suitcase, umbrella, fish tank, storeroom) are made up for the task. In practice a real umbrella has thickness, which makes fitting harder. running: - "Predict: show of hands. Those who chose 'no, it's longer than every side' haven't thought about the diagonal. Those who chose 'yes, 80 + 50 + 30' have added the sides." - "Run: before anyone moves a slider, ask which side of the box is the longest line you can fit." - "Paper: the fish tank try-one after the worked example and the suitcase in Make are worked on paper first. Look for the floor triangle drawn first." - "Modify: for the cube, ask whether the answer will be more or less than twice a side." stuck: - see: A student adds 80 + 50 + 30. ask: Is the shortest path across a box along the edges or straight across? fix: "Straight across: use Pythagoras, floor first and then the standing triangle." - see: A student adds the floor diagonal and the height. ask: Is the standing triangle right-angled? Which side is the hypotenuse? fix: "The space diagonal. Use Pythagoras again: square, add, square root." - see: A student gets 28.3 for √(80² + 50²) on a calculator. ask: Did you square each side first, then add? fix: Square each, add, then take the square root of the total. stretch: What is the longest straight line inside the classroom? Measure the room, predict, and calculate. support: A printed box with the floor triangle and the standing triangle drawn in two colours. leads: > Finishes AC9M10M03. Where it leads: solids in Year 10 measurement, where the same triangle gives heights and slant lengths. exit: q: A box is 6 cm by 6 cm by 7 cm. What is the longest straight line inside it? a: 11 cm (36 + 36 + 49 = 121). explain: > To find a length inside a box, find a right-angled triangle. The floor gives one: its hypotenuse is the floor diagonal. Then the floor diagonal and the height are the shorter sides of a second triangle, standing up. Its hypotenuse is the longest line in the box: $\sqrt{l^2 + w^2 + h^2}$. ```

# Boards for "The triangle inside". The space3d board's diagonal view: a box from the origin to P, with the floor
# diagonal and the space diagonal and the standing right-angled triangle shaded.

size: 6

files.working.txt:
# Sam's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: sam
The floor of the suitcase is 80 cm by 50 cm, so its diagonal is √(80² + 50²) = 94.3 cm.
The second triangle has the floor diagonal and the 30 cm height as its shorter sides.
So the longest line is 94.3 + 30 = 124.3 cm.
124.3 is longer than 120, so the umbrella fits.
# endregion
